title: Edit the array
intro: Instructions count positions from 1 (first, second, fourth…), but indexes count from 0. Click the box each instruction means, and watch the code fill in its index.

rounds.right: Positions count from 1 and indexes from 0, so an element's index is always one less than its position.

why.click: That's `{clicked}`, the {clickedOrdinal} element. Indexes start at 0, so an element's index is one less than its position.

rounds.right: `.length` is the number of boxes, {length}. The last index is one less: {last}.

why.length: `.length` counts the boxes the way you'd count them on your fingers, starting at 1. It's the last index that is one less.

rounds.right: The last element is always at index `{name}.length - 1`, here {last}.

why.last: That's `{clicked}`. The last element sits at index `{name}.length - 1`.
why.copy: {chosen} is in `{chosenExpr}`, the {chosenOrdinal} element. Which index holds {source}?

rounds.right: Indexes run from 0 to `{name}.length - 1`. After your edits, `{name}` is `{array}`.

why.lastIndex: The first element is index 0, so the indexes of {length} boxes run from 0 up to one less than {length}.
